findings.defect: In sunlight the flown capsule is a brushed-brass bell, not a charred spacecraft. Under the chutes the lit cone and the forward bay are an even warm bronze, three times as bright as the unlit side, with straight evenly spaced light and dark streaks from rim to apex that read as brushed or anodised metal; at 5x the streak edges are staircases. No mottle, crackle, flaked patch or run that starts at a fitting. In the lab's charred view the cone has the brightness of the pristine one (luma 77), tinted khaki, and the bay's lid is clean bright chrome. The unlit half is a convincing near-black, so the two halves of one picture (the lee view) disagree about what the surface is.
findings.realReference: out/qa/ref/spacecraft-hardware/dragon-demo1-postflight.jpg: matte near-black to dark brown, mottled, with a crackle, white patches where char came away, brown runs of different width from fittings and a paler nose; nothing on it shines. out/qa/ref/reentry-chutes/artemis2-mains.jpg and soyuz-ms24-landing.jpg: under its canopies the capsule is a dark matte shape even in full sun.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/core/mesh/meshSystem.ts:214-219: sootDensity = weight x (0.67 + 0.66 x streaks), so every other streak cell falls back to two thirds of the weight; there the albedo is the film times the warm veil (0.42, 0.38, 0.33) and metallic is only taken out between density 0.15 and 0.9, so 'shell-tape' (metallic 0.82, src/render/vehicle/materials.ts:110) keeps a brown metallic lobe: brass in direct light, black where only the sky lights it. The streak cells (0.06 x 1.5) are regular and full length. The apex cover is a lathe in its own material with constant masks (src/render/vehicle/parts/capsule.ts:885-905) and does not take the cone's scorch field. The lab's charred state seems to drive a lower instance soot than the game's (vesselFeature.ts:313).
findings.fixDirection: Core: any visible deposit hides the mirror: metallic to 0 and roughness to 0.9 by density 0.3; a neutral veil (about 0.30, 0.30, 0.30 times the base) with brown only as a narrow band at the deposit's thin edge; streak modulation of plus or minus 15 per cent, so thick soot stays thick. Vehicle-pad: a low-frequency mottle and a few pale flaked patches in the capsule's scorch field, streaks of 2-20 cm width and 0.2-2 m length that start at fittings, plugs and tile corners; soot the lid, its seal band and the bay from the same field (or fly the chute phase without the lid, see finding 23); drive the lab's charred view with the game's value. Acceptance in tests/browser/vehicle/game.spec.ts: sunlit cone in qa-drogues at most luma 45 with R minus B at most 15 (now 94 and 69), and at most half the luminance of the same view with a pristine capsule.

findings.fixDirection: Ring main: grey zinc with white scale blooms and rust only at flanges, welds and under the heads; bolted flanges every 3-4 m, saddles and U-bolts; bronze or stainless nozzle heads with a slot. Bells: heat tint and a darker lip. Arms: quick-disconnect plates with collars, jacketed flex hoses with frost, drip trays, cable bundles. White room: a bellows to the hatch, lights, placards, door hardware. Tower: a clad lift shaft on one face, pipe risers and trays up another, boxes and hose reels per level, rust from the gussets down; vary every third level.

From 10-30 m the silver blankets are hammered chrome: smooth decimetre dents that swing from white to near black like a funhouse mirror. findings.realReference: out/qa/ref/spacecraft-hardware/lm-challenger-orbit.jpg and lm-spider.jpg: flat facets with sharp fine creases, a broad dull sheen, panels of different tone and tilt, taped seams, black and aluminium panels mixed. out/qa/ref/moon-surface/lm-falcon-lrv.jpg: crinkled gold and black foil with hard creases, torn and taped edges, dust on the lower parts.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/vehicle/materials.ts:117-118: 'mli-gold' and 'mli-silver' are metals (0.88, 0.92) at roughness 0.5-0.56 under normal maps whose strongest band is a smooth 10-25 cm undulation (tools/vehicle/bake-textures.ts, mli_n and mlisilver_n); the roughness does not rise with the normal variance in the mips, so at distance the dents stay mirror-sharp; one material instance per blanket with no per-panel tone or tilt; radiator, tanks and quads are single primitives in src/render/vehicle/parts/lander.ts.
findings.fixDirection: Rebuild the fold layer as a ridged crease network (straight creases 1-5 cm apart with flat facets between them) and cut the smooth low band to a quarter; fold normal variance into roughness per mip so panels converge to a dull sheen with small glints; tone and tilt steps per panel, kapton tape along seams, snaps, overlapping lips as geometry at LOD 0, a few black or painted panels. Louvres or tubes on the radiator, straps and lines on the tanks, a modelled quad. After touchdown a grey dust weight on the lower third (see finding 21).

findings.defect: Frost is told now, but close up it is an even translucent white veil, not ice. LOX, the roundel and the placard show through it at one reduced contrast everywhere, like fogged film. The bare lanes are ruler-straight grey bars of constant width from ring to ring with a step at each weld, and one of them crosses the CAUTION CRYOGENIC placard, so its left fifth is yellow and the rest is veiled. The coat has no grain, thickness, runnels or sparkle; the top edge is a blurred scalloped band.
findings.realReference: out/qa/ref/launch-pad/apollo15-saturnv-from-ml.jpg: frosted sections are dead matte and opaque. Frost builds thickest at tank bottoms and weld lands, sheds in irregular plates, and markings vanish under it or show through ragged thin patches, never through an even veil.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/core/mesh/meshSystem.ts:224-229: frostCover = smoothstep(0, 0.6, weight x (0.75 + 0.5 x streaks)) is a plain mix of albedo toward (0.90, 0.94, 1.0) with roughness 0.95: no normal, thickness or glint term, so a weight below full cover is a veil. The weights in src/render/vehicle/parts/stage.ts are per-vertex plateaus (0.75 and above on the coat, 0.12 in the lanes) interpolated between rings; the markings model takes one even weight.
findings.fixDirection: Core: treat the weight as a thickness: opaque above a noise threshold that falls with thickness (ragged plate edges instead of a blend), a bump from the thickness, a sparse sparkle at grazing sun. Vehicle-pad: break the lanes into irregular plates and runs keyed to a 0.3-1 m noise, keep them off placards, let lettering disappear where the coat is thick, thicken toward tank bottoms and ring frames.

findings.likelyCause: src/render/vehicle/site/ground.ts:298-341: the whole cross-section sits on one height per row (under = ground.hi at the centre line) and only the two toe vertices drop to ground.lo minus FOOT_COVER, so the outer quad becomes a near-vertical skirt wherever the ground falls across the 2.3 h base; half = base x max(0.12, k) keeps 12 per cent of the width at the ends while the height goes to zero; the rendered terrain at that spot lies lower than the site's ground field.
findings.fixDirection: Height per vertex: y = ground(x, z) + h x k x bell, with the bell's slope carried 0.5 m below the lowest ground instead of a skirt; let the width go to zero on a rounded plan; a grime and fines ramp over the last metre; ask the terrain for a levelled footprint under berms as under roads. Add an assertion that no berm vertex above ground has a neighbour more than 0.4 m below the terrain.
